Sound Familiar?

Common Infectious Disease Billing Problems

Each problem below is one PMEX resolves before it costs you revenue.

High-cost antibiotic J-code submitted at vial size, not administered dose quantity.

PMEX verifies drug quantity from the infusion nursing record and bills the correct J-code units on every infusion claim.

Inpatient ID consultation billed as a subsequent visit, losing the higher consultation rate.

PMEX applies the correct initial consultation framework per payer for every first ID contact on an admitted patient.

HIV management visit coded at low complexity when the multi-problem MDM supports higher.

PMEX codes HIV management E/M from 2021 MDM criteria, capturing the full complexity of multi-diagnosis management.

Prior authorization for specialty antifungals not obtained before the course starts.

PMEX manages anti-infective prior authorization and tracks renewal windows per patient per drug course.

Telehealth ID visit submitted without modifier 95, adjudicated at wrong rate.

PMEX applies modifier 95 and confirms payer-specific telehealth coverage before every remote ID visit claim.

Infusion administration codes not billed alongside antibiotic J-codes.

PMEX submits infusion administration CPT codes (96365 to 96368) alongside every drug J-code on infusion claims.

Denial Management

Top Denial Patterns in Infectious Disease Billing

Infectious disease practices lose 16 to 24 percent of revenue to drug quantity errors, consultation miscoding, and authorization gaps on specialty agents.

PATTERN 01

Antibiotic Drug Quantity Billed at Vial Size

Patient receives 2g ceftriaxone IV. J0696 is billed per 250mg. Correct units: 8. Billing team submits 4 (one vial). Half the drug revenue lost on every infusion visit with this error pattern.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX calculates J-code billing units from the administered dose in the infusion nursing record, converting grams to milligrams and dividing by the per-unit descriptor on every antibiotic infusion claim.

PATTERN 02

ID Consultation Billed as Subsequent Visit

Infectious disease specialist sees a new inpatient referral. Bills 99232 (subsequent hospital visit) instead of the appropriate initial consultation level. Revenue difference: $60 to $120 per consult depending on complexity. Applies to every new inpatient ID referral.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX identifies every first-contact inpatient ID evaluation and codes the correct initial consultation level based on the documented history, examination, and medical decision-making complexity.

PATTERN 03

Specialty Antifungal Denied, Authorization Not On File

Patient started on IV micafungin for invasive candidiasis. No prior authorization obtained. Commercial payer denies the drug claim at $480 per day. Retroactive authorization not available under the payer contract.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX manages prior authorization for all high-cost IV anti-infective agents, confirming authorization is active before the first dose is administered and tracking renewal for extended treatment courses.

Questions

Infectious Disease Billing Questions Answered

We apply the correct initial consultation framework based on the payer. For Medicare, inpatient consultations are billed as initial hospital care (99221 to 99223). For commercial payers that recognize consultation codes, we use 99251 to 99255.

We verify the administered dose from the infusion nursing record, calculate the correct J-code billing units, and submit the drug J-code alongside the infusion administration CPT code (96365 for first hour, 96366 for additional hours).

Yes. HIV patients with two or more chronic conditions may qualify for CCM (99490 or 99487) when clinical staff time meets the monthly threshold and patient consent is on file.

We obtain prior authorization before the treatment course begins, attach the required clinical documentation including culture results and treatment rationale, and track renewal dates for extended courses.

Yes. We manage the full billing workflow for ID practices across inpatient consultation, outpatient clinic, and infusion center settings.
